model_annotation:
Both diagrams share the same x-axis, labeled with years ranging from 1995 to 2020 in five-year intervals, and display two y-axes. The left y-axis represents the "IWF Fiskalindex" (IMF Fiscal Index) on a linear scale from 0 to 2.5 in the left diagram and from -5 to 2 in the right diagram, with tick labels at intervals of 0.5. The right y-axis represents "Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat" (Total Government Debt Ratio) in the left diagram, scaled from 60 to 120, and "Schuldenquote Zentralstaat" (Central Government Debt Ratio) in the right diagram, scaled from 30 to 70, both with tick labels at intervals of 10. 

The left diagram illustrates the IMF Fiscal Index and Total Government Debt Ratio over time, featuring three lines: a blue line representing the IMF Fiscal Index, marked with blue triangles, a purple line for the Total Government Debt Ratio, marked with red triangles, and no other lines are present in this diagram. The blue line starts at approximately 0.1 in 1995, peaks at around 1 in 2010, and then declines to about 0.5 by 2020, with a slight increase to 0.7 between 2019 and 2020. The purple line begins at around 60 in 1995, remains relatively stable until 2008, then sharply increases to around 100 by 2015, and further to approximately 110 by 2020.

The right diagram displays the IMF Fiscal Index and Central Government Debt Ratio, with the same blue and purple lines and corresponding triangle markers. The blue line starts at around -2 in 1995, peaks at approximately 0.5 in 2010, and then declines to about -0.5 by 2019 before slightly increasing to around -0.25 by 2020. The purple line begins at around 36 in 1995, remains relatively stable until 2008, then rises to approximately 55 by 2014, and further to around 65 by 2020.
